# auto-deploy

> Deployment service for Linux/systemd hosts. If you are an AI agent working in an application repository that deploys here, this file tells you how to build a CI/CD pipeline this server will accept: publish a GitHub Release whose asset is a raw Linux ELF binary named exactly as configured, then POST the tag to /webhook.

Version: {{VERSION}}
Repository: https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go
Full context: /llms-full.txt

Read the sections in order. The artifact contract is where pipelines usually break,
and three of the values you need are configured per application in this server's
admin UI — ask the repository owner for them rather than guessing.

## This host

Every application this server deploys runs on this same machine, so every artifact
must target the platform below. These values are read from the running server process
itself: it is an ELF binary the kernel here agreed to execute, so a binary built the
same way will run too.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| GOOS | `{{GOOS}}` |
| GOARCH | `{{GOARCH}}` |
| `uname -m` / `file` reports | `{{ARCH_UNAME}}` |
| Rust target triple | `{{RUST_TARGET}}` |

Build command for a Go project — the `-o` name must be the app's configured artifact
name, which is the one value still to ask the owner for:

```bash
GOOS={{GOOS}} GOARCH={{GOARCH}} CGO_ENABLED=0 \
  go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o <ARTIFACT_NAME> ./cmd/app
```

Do not publish a multi-arch matrix. One application maps to exactly one artifact name,
so a second architecture would have to overwrite the same asset.

## Sections

- [Read this first](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/01-overview.md): You are most likely an AI agent working in an application repository whose owner deploys through this auto-deploy instance. Your job is to produce a CI/CD pipeline this server will accept — this document states exactly what it requires.
- [Artifact contract — the part that breaks pipelines](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/02-artifact-contract.md): The release asset must be a raw, uncompressed Linux ELF executable, published under a filename that matches the app's configured artifact name exactly, and no larger than 100 MiB.
- [The pipeline to generate](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/03-cicd-recipe.md): Build for Linux, publish the release with the asset named exactly as configured, then call the webhook — in that order. Treat HTTP 200 (`duplicate`) as success alongside 202.
- [Webhook reference](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/04-webhook-contract.md): `POST /webhook` with `Authorization: Bearer <app-token>` and `{"tag": "v1.2.3"}`. 202 means queued, 200 means the same tag is already in flight, and neither means the deploy succeeded.
- [Failure symptoms and their causes](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/05-troubleshooting.md): Most failures are the artifact contract, not the pipeline. Map the symptom to the cause here before changing the workflow.
- [Server configuration (operator reference)](https://github.com/izzamoe/auto-deploy-and-refresh-go/blob/master/docs/llms/06-server-configuration.md): Not needed to write a pipeline. This is for whoever runs the auto-deploy instance itself: process-level settings come from environment variables, per-application settings live in SQLite and are edited through the admin UI.

## Endpoints reachable from your pipeline

| Method | Path | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/llms-full.txt` | public |
| GET | `/llms.txt` | public |
| POST | `/webhook` | bearer token |

Everything under `/admin` requires an admin session cookie and is not usable from CI.
The complete route table is in /llms-full.txt.
